title: Critical Sensing with Autonomous Devices: The Self-Oscillation Threshold of a Frequency-Locked NV-Centre Magnetometer
authors: Joan Toledo Aguilera, Gonzalo Reina Rivero, Marcel Morillas-Rozas, Javier Cerrillo
abstract: Feedback locking of a probe frequency to a spin resonance is the standard operating mode of precision quantum sensors. Here we deliberately operate such a lock outside its stable regime: a continuous-wave nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensemble magnetometer, frequency-modulation (FM) locked to one flank of its optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), is driven through the flip (period-doubling) bifurcation of its discrete feedback map by raising the software loop gain $G$. Beyond a critical gain $\Gc$ the lock becomes a self-sustained oscillator whose limit cycle is generated by the loop itself. We derive the threshold condition $\Gc = 2\,\Dcal/\Dtrue$, which identifies the measurable content of the threshold: the ratio of the transduction slope of the ODMR lock-in signal at calibration time $D_{cal}$ to its value at present $D_{true}$. We present an identifiability analysis showing which physical parameters this single scalar can and cannot distinguish, characterize the estimators of $\Gc$ under realistic noise, and report measurements on our current setup: an experimental bifurcation diagram with onset at $\Gc \approx 2$ as predicted for a self-calibrated loop, sub-threshold critical fluctuations following the predicted $\sqrt{G/(2-G)}$ divergence.
summary: The researchers studied a frequency-locked NV magnetometer by intentionally driving its feedback loop past its stable operational point. They modeled this using a discrete map exhibiting a period-doubling bifurcation, predicting an oscillation onset at $G_c=2$. Experimentally, they confirmed this transition, demonstrating the system's ability to self-oscillate and characterizing the approach to this critical threshold.
main_problem: The study investigates autonomous self-oscillating behavior in a frequency-locked Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centre magnetometer by deliberately operating the lock outside its stable regime.
main_result: The experiment successfully confirmed the theoretical prediction that the onset of self-oscillation occurs at a critical gain $G_c \approx 2.0$, validating the model's description of the flip bifurcation in the feedback loop.
method: The authors employed continuous measurements on an NV magnetometer, analyzing the system dynamics by driving the frequency lock through a period-doubling (flip) bifurcation using software control.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a Continuous-Wave ODMR ensemble magnetometer. The operation is modeled as a one-dimensional discrete map whose stability and bifurcations are controlled by adjusting the dimensionless loop gain $G$.
key_observables: Coherent period-2 amplitude ($a_2$), sub-threshold orbit spread ($\sigma_f(G)$), and the critical gain threshold ($G_c$).
important_parameters: Loop gain ($G$), calibration slope ($D_{	ext{cal}}$), true operating slope ($D_{	ext{true}}$), and the bifurcation point $G_c$.
main_assumptions: The nonlinearity is implemented in software after digitization, which limits its metrological advantage compared to physical nonlinearities.
figures_summary: Figures summarize measurements showing the jump in coherent period-2 amplitude ($a_2$) around $G \approx 1.8-2.2$, and the divergence of the orbit spread following the predicted $\propto 1/(2 - G)$ trend.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical model based on a discrete map, derives the critical threshold condition ($G_c$), performs identifiability analysis, and concludes with experimental measurements confirming the bifurcation onset and divergence behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides an excellent example of using nonlinear dynamics (bifurcation theory) to characterize and control a quantum sensor's operating regime, moving beyond simple linear sensing modes into controlled non-equilibrium dynamics.
